page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor using the 64-bit ARM64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, operating without hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and a built-in 474 GB NVMe SSD local instance store. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several compute and memory operations. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.88 and a multi-core score of 12133.14. Memory bandwidth is measured at 473.11 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 116.89 GB/sec for large-block reads. However, single-threaded performance shows limitations, with a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and weak results in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Cryptographic performance is also lower, with a Passmark encryption score of 1084.81, though hardware-accelerated AES is present.

Given its dedicated ARM cores and local NVMe storage, the c6gd.2xlarge offers qualitative resource density for workloads requiring local scratch space and balanced multi-core execution. It demonstrates solid capabilities in database operations, scoring 5269.76 on Passmark database benchmarks and handling 9.43 million Redis SET operations per second. Static web serving throughput is also stable at 9.78 GB/sec. This instance is best suited for multi-threaded applications, web serving, database nodes utilizing local storage, and software compilation tasks, while being less optimal for single-threaded compute or heavy LLM inference workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized, ARM64-based instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs without hyperthreading, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a 474 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark results show average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and a Redis SET throughput of 9.43 million operations per second, though single-threaded and cryptographic performance are relatively weak. The inclusion of local NVMe storage combined with dedicated ARM cores makes this instance highly suitable for database operations, multi-threaded web serving, and software compilation workloads that benefit from low-latency local scratch space.
